lessons.title: Non-Fiction: The United Kingdom
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about the UK from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about the UK.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children know about the UK.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple non-fiction text about the UK.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions about the UK.
key_questions: What countries make up the UK?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about the UK.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about the UK at home.

lessons.title: Number Consolidation: Counting Flags
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count and represent numbers to 20 using a UK-themed context.
success_criteria: I can count UK-themed objects.
I can write the numeral.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting UK-themed counters (mini flags, red/white/blue counters), recording numerals.
lessons.independent_task: Children count sets of UK-themed counters up to 20, recording numerals.
key_questions: How many flags in this set?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy consolidation — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Count red, white and blue objects at home.

lessons.title: The Four Countries of the UK
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name the four countries of the UK and their capital cities.
success_criteria: I can name the four UK countries.
I can name a capital city.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the four countries of the UK and their capital cities (London, Edinburgh, Cardiff, Belfast).
lessons.independent_task: Children label the four countries and capitals on a UK map outline.
key_questions: What is the capital of Scotland?

differentiation.greater_depth: Label all 4 countries and capitals independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note locational knowledge of the UK — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the four countries and capitals.
lessons.home_link: Find the UK countries on a map together.

lessons.title: Who Is the King/Queen? Our Monarchy
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a simple fact about the UK monarchy.
success_criteria: I can name the current monarch.
I can say one thing about their role.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children know about royalty.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the role of the monarch simply and factually, using current, accurate information.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and record a fact about the monarchy.
key_questions: Who is the monarch of the UK?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall of a significant national institution — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about the monarchy with your family.

lessons.title: Writing About My Country
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write factual sentences about the UK or a UK country.
success_criteria: I can write a fact about the UK.
I can use a capital letter and full stop.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a factual sentence about the UK or one of its countries.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 factual sentences about the UK.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note factual writing progress — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family a fact about the UK.

lessons.title: Comparing Distances Between UK Cities
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare distances using a simple UK map scale.
success_criteria: I can say which journey looks longer.
I can order 3 journeys by distance.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing distances between UK cities using a simplified map.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare and order given UK city-to-city journeys by approximate distance.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note distance comparison applied to UK geography — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Look at distances between places you know on a map.

lessons.title: National Symbols of the UK
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name a national symbol for each UK country.
success_criteria: I can name a symbol (flower, flag) for a UK country.
I can match it to the correct country.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at UK national symbols (rose, thistle, daffodil, shamrock).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce national symbols/flowers of each UK country.
lessons.independent_task: Children match national symbols to their UK country, recording their matching.
key_questions: What is the symbol of Wales?
Which country does the thistle represent?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note cultural/locational knowledge — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Look for a UK national symbol on something at home (e.g. a coin).

lessons.title: Our School and Local Area: Then and Now
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one change in their local area over time.
success_criteria: I can say one thing that has changed locally.
I can say how I know.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss the local area and what children notice.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss using old photos/maps (if available) to spot changes in the local area over time.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw or discuss one change they've noticed or been told about in their local area.
key_questions: What has changed near your home/school?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for why the change happened

lessons.assessment_notes: Note local history/change over time understanding, linking to living memory — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Ask a family member about a local change they remember.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading UK-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read UK-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read UK words.
I can read a sentence about the UK.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending UK-themed words (e.g. 'flag', 'king', 'land').
lessons.independent_task: Children read UK-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading UK-themed words over the week.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Addition and Subtraction Consolidation
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to consolidate addition and subtraction skills within 20.
success_criteria: I can add within 20.
I can subtract within 20.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies used across the year.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of key strategies (number lines, counters, number bonds).
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a mixed addition/subtraction consolidation worksheet.
lessons.assessment_notes: End-of-term consolidation check on addition/subtraction — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising addition and subtraction over the week.

lessons.title: Weather Around the UK
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe typical UK weather using geographical vocabulary.
success_criteria: I can describe UK weather.
I can use a weather word.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss typical UK weather patterns (often rainy/cloudy, four distinct seasons) using a simple weather map.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a simple UK weather forecast using symbols and vocabulary.
key_questions: What is the weather like today?
What weather symbol would you use?

differentiation.support: Use symbols with word bank support
differentiation.greater_depth: Present a detailed forecast for multiple UK regions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note weather vocabulary and geographical application — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Watch or listen to a real weather forecast with your family.

lessons.title: Presenting a UK Country
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present facts about a chosen UK country clearly.
success_criteria: I can share a fact about my chosen country.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear country presentation (capital, symbol, fact).
lessons.independent_task: Children choose a UK country and present 2-3 facts about it to a small group.
resources_needed: Work from the week for reference

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and geographical knowledge recall — evidence for ENG.SL1/GEOG.1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all the UK country presentations.
lessons.home_link: Present your chosen UK country to your family.

lessons.title: Position and Direction: UK Map Journey
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a journey on a UK map using positional language.
success_criteria: I can describe a journey using direction words.
I can say where a place is relative to another.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap directions and turns from earlier terms.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce simple compass directions (north, south, east, west) using a UK map.
lessons.independent_task: Children describe simple journeys between UK cities using directional language.
key_questions: Is Scotland north or south of England?

differentiation.greater_depth: Use all four compass directions confidently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record early compass direction understanding — evidence for MATHS.GEO/GEOG.1 links.
lessons.home_link: Find north on a map or compass app together.

lessons.title: Comparing Our Local Area to Another UK Place
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare their local area to another place in the UK.
success_criteria: I can name one thing about my local area.
I can compare it to another UK place.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing the local area (city/town/village) to a contrasting UK location (e.g. rural vs urban).
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a simple comparison chart of their local area vs another UK place.
resources_needed: pictures of a contrasting UK location
key_questions: What is different about this place?

differentiation.support: Complete with adult support, one similarity/difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative geographical thinking about places — evidence for GEOG.1/GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Share comparisons made with the class.
lessons.home_link: Talk about somewhere different in the UK you've visited or heard of.

lessons.title: UK Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about the UK.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about the UK, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What are the four countries of the UK?
Why might UK weather change often?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on UK facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Full Term Consolidation
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply a range of maths skills learned this term in a mixed challenge.
success_criteria: I can count, add and subtract confidently.
I can apply measuring and shape skills.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap key maths vocabulary from the term.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the term's core maths content.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a mixed review worksheet covering the term's key skills.

differentiation.support: Complete with reduced complexity and support

lessons.assessment_notes: End of Spring term maths consolidation summary for each child.
lessons.home_link: Review the term's maths learning together.

lessons.title: United Kingdom Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about the UK learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name the four UK countries and capitals.
I can name a UK symbol.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about the UK.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Our United Kingdom' display combining maps, symbols, and country presentations from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about the UK?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning, completing Spring 1 — evidence for GEOG.1/GEOG.2/HIST.1/HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished 'Our United Kingdom' display, celebrating the end of Spring 1.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about the UK with your family.
